findings.claim: GeneratedFormatterCollector.GetInstanceMembers walks the base type chain and CreateMember sets DeclaringType = null, so members inherited from a base class are generated. Contractless mode also produces string keys sorted ordinally, while the dynamic ContractlessStandardResolver orders by declaration. A user who later switches between the dynamic and generated formatters would see different map layouts and member sets. Also, the contractless mode here skips get-only members, which ContractlessStandardResolver includes.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a sample type with public props B, A and a public get-only prop C using ContractlessStandardResolver and a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter; compare the bytes (key order and member set).

findings.claim: New analyzer diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added as Errors, but I see no corresponding AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md entry in the diff. This makes the build emit RS2000 (release tracking) warnings, which become errors under warnings-as-errors for the analyzer project and downstream. The new diagnostics also have no doc pages for their help links.

receipt_plan.detail: Build MessagePack.SourceGenerator with release tracking enabled and check for RS2000/RS2002 warnings; check that doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md exists.

findings.claim: The diagnostics collector runs through generatedFormatterDiagnostics, which is wired via RegisterSourceOutput to report diagnostics. GeneratorUtilities now excludes any class that has the attribute from the hand-written formatter list. The exclusion happens even when the class is rejected (not partial, wrong interface) and produces no model. As a result the formatter silently drops out of the resolver too, but only for users who opted in with the new attribute, so the impact is limited.

receipt_plan.detail: Apply [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] to a non-partial formatter class and run the generator snapshot test; check that the resolver output and diagnostics are as intended.
